title: Mexican Hot Casserole Dish
description: This is a “no-recipe” recipe, a recipe without an ingredients list or steps (though I’ve intervened a little). It invites you to improvise in the kitchen. Sam Sifton has been cooking enchiladas con carne ever since Robb Walsh taught him how to make them in the kitchen of his El Real Tex-Mex Cafe in Houston. Enchiladas can be a drag to assemble. So do as the New Mexicans do, and stack rather than roll.
ingredients: 1 pound of ground beef (or some similar mixture)
1 or more dashes of chili powder, ground cumin, oregano
Chopped onions, sour cream, and salsa on the side
directions: Sauté a pound or so of ground meat in a splash of oil, with a little flour and a pinch of salt, then set it in another dish.
Use the same pan to cook chopped onion, garlic, and jalapeño, 3 to 4 minutes.
Return the meat to the pan, and hit it with chili powder, ground cumin, and oregano, to taste.
Add chopped tomatoes and a little water to loosen everything up. Let it reduce a little.
Using a casserole dish, put a little of the above chili in the bottom of the casserole, warm my tortillas in a dry skillet and lay them across the chili as if building the first layer of a lasagna.
Then do it that again and again, and finish with the remaining chili and cheese.
Bake in the oven until everything’s bubbling, 5 to 10 minutes.
Serve with chopped raw onions, sour cream, and salsa on the side.
